description: Original floyd_warshall tests with independent oracle.
state: deterministic terminating candidate return tables on this fixed finite fixture schedule, with four test verdicts
forward: The fixed four-test schedule maps candidate returns to exact assertion verdicts. Four tests: 19,768 directed graphs with 0..3 vertices and each arc absent/weight0/weight3; 48 seeded graphs with 4..6 vertices and full-width/MAX weights (seed 0xf10d20261029); boundary/parallel/zero-cycle/wide-sum fixtures; transpose plus duplicate/reordered arcs and factor7 scaling. Enumerate every simple path by bounded recursive DFS and minimize costs per target, including the empty path. Since weights are nonnegative, deleting cycles cannot increase cost, so simple paths suffice. The oracle does not invoke Dijkstra, Floyd recurrence or production code.
inverse: Declare U as all deterministic terminating candidate return tables on this fixed fixture schedule crossed with four pass/fail verdicts. R is assertion evaluation. U minus R excludes passing when any executed assertion disagrees with its independent expected value, and excludes failure when all assertions pass. Exact assertion specification; actual Rust correspondence is partial. Compilation failure, timeout and resource failure are outside U.

Pre(y) retains ALL candidate return tables whose assertions produce observed verdicts y. Pass constrains only tested calls, leaving untested inputs arbitrary. Failure preserves every compatible first failing assertion and earlier passing returns. No unique source implementation follows from these observations.
cost: Simple-path enumeration is factorial in vertex count, deliberately bounded: exhaustive V<=3 and48 seeded graphs V<=6. Recursion depth <=6 for generated oracle calls; small transformed fixture V=5. Production matrix remains O(V^2).
checks: four targeted tests twice; strict Clippy; compiled filtered mutation
limitations: Bounded correspondence is not unrestricted proof.
Partial syntax excludes macro expansion and semantic resolution.
